questions.text: Within ten seconds of opening the page, what do you think this product does and who is it for? Answer before reading closely.
Earmark claims money can only reach the destination it was locked to and can never be redirected by a person in the middle. How convincingly does the page prove that claim?
You are being asked to put real money through this. What specifically would stop you trusting it, and what evidence would remove that doubt?
Open a drive page at /d/1. Is it unambiguous what you would be paying, to whom, and what happens after you pay? Name anything that is unclear.
Rate the experience on a phone screen, which is where nearly every real user will see this.

The product collects one shared bill from a group chat and pays it directly to a school, landlord or vendor. Does the page explain that job better than a generic crypto payments page would, or does it read as interchangeable?
